candidates.title: Activation Sparsity with Weight Approximation for Faster LLM Decoding on Offloaded Weights
candidates.abstract: Deploying LLMs on consumer-grade GPUs with insufficient memory to hold their weights can result in prohibitively slow inference, because decoding repeatedly transfers offloaded weights from system RAM or flash storage into GPU at much lower bandwidth than local GPU-memory access. Activation sparsity reduces these transfers by skipping weights associated with zero or near-zero activations. However, as more activation contributions are omitted, model quality eventually degrades rapidly, indicating that weights associated with small-magnitude activations collectively influence model quality sharply. In this work, we improve the trade-off between model quality and decoding performance when exploiting activation sparsity. Our key idea is to replace the binary choice of whether or not to read a weight with three options: fully retain it, approximate it using a compressed weight representation, or omit it entirely. SpAx skips weights associated with activations closest to zero, reads approximate weights for smaller-magnitude activations, and reads original weights for the largest-magnitude activations. Smaller-magnitude activations attenuate the errors introduced by approximate weights, while compressed weight representations require fewer bytes to be transferred. With weights offloaded to CPU memory, SpAx speeds up decoding by 3.86X on average (up to 5.57X) with 16-bit weights and 2.06X (up to 2.74X) with 4-bit weights, at a WikiText-2 perplexity increase of at most 10%. With weights offloaded to flash storage, the speedups are 3.31X on average (up to 4.81X) and 1.54X (up to 2.03X).
candidates.reason: SpAxはCPU RAM/flashへ重みをoffloadしたLLMで、activationの小さい行に対応する重みを完全取得・圧縮近似取得・省略の3段階で選ぶ。小さなactivationでは重み近似誤差の影響が弱いことを利用し、CPU offloadで16bit平均3.86倍、4bit平均2.06倍のdecode高速化、flash offloadで16bit平均3.31倍を報告。WikiText-2 perplexity増加は最大10%という品質コストに注意。

candidates.title: EdgeAgent: Orchestrating On-Device LLM inference for End-User Multi-Agent Systems on CPU-GPU Unified Memory Architectures
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM International Conference on Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems, Volume 1
candidates.abstract: Emerging multi-agent LLMs demand privacy-preserving edge deployment, yet current inference systems struggle with these collaborative workflows. Specifically, the memory-bound decode phase causes severe bus contention on unified memory architectures (UMA), paralyzing naive CPU-GPU co-execution. Furthermore, speculative decoding in multi-agent workloads faces extreme variance in drafting difficulty, alternating between complex reasoning and predictable structured generation. Compounded by frequent tool-induced stalls, this highly fragmented execution severely underutilizes hardware and defeats traditional static batching. We present EdgeAgent, a cross-layer inference system explicitly co-designed for edge UMA and multi-agent workloads. At the micro-architectural level, it bypasses rigid graph-compiler constraints to enable zero-copy UMA-aware tensor parallelism, utilizing asymmetric memory layouts to fully saturate both CPU and GPU compute units. At the scheduling level, it dynamically allocates draft budgets based on real-time sequence predictability to bound bandwidth waste. Concurrently, an asynchronous suspend-and-yield mechanism actively evicts stalled agents, ensuring continuous hardware saturation during unpredictable tool invocations. Extensive evaluations on an Apple M4 SoC demonstrate that the UMA-aware execution alone contributes a 1.29× speedup over batched speculative decoding. Adding the agent-aware scheduling lifts the full EdgeAgent system to a 1.77× speedup under extreme tool-use latencies.
candidates.reason: EdgeAgentはApple M4等のCPU/GPU統合メモリ環境で、decodeのバス競合とエージェントtool待機を同時に扱う。UMA-aware zero-copy tensor parallelism、draft難易度に応じた投機予算制御、停止中agentの非同期suspend-and-yieldを組み合わせる。M4評価で実行方式のみで1.29倍、tool待機が多い条件で全体1.77倍の高速化を報告。

candidates.title: Parallel Language Models via Variational Decoding
candidates.abstract: Autoregressive language models emit one token per forward pass. This causes high inference latency, in particular as models are scaled up for quality. In this paper, we introduce Parallel Language Models (PLMs), which generate mutually consistent tokens in one forward pass by routing dependencies through latent auxiliary variables. PLMs are trained using a variational bound that reduces to an autoregressive loss plus a parallel decoding loss. Empirically, PLMs are on a faster and better Pareto frontier than autoregressive and discrete diffusion baselines. Pretrained PLMs achieve near-autoregressive pretraining loss on model scales of 80M to 3B parameters, and speedup follows a power law in model size. When post-trained, our 1.3B model matches or exceeds an identically trained autoregressive model on math, coding, and instruction-following benchmarks, speeding up inference $2.3\text{-}5.7\times$. Together, we show that parallel generation can be trained from a single training objective at autoregressive quality. We will make our code available at https://github.com/mandt-lab/plm.
candidates.reason: Parallel Language Modelsは潜在補助変数を通じてtoken間依存を伝播させ、1 forwardで相互整合する複数tokenを生成する。自己回帰損失と並列decode損失を含む変分下界で学習し、80M～3Bの事前学習モデルで品質と速度のPareto改善を示す。1.3Bのpost-trainingモデルで数理・coding・指示追従品質を保ちながら推論2.3～5.7倍高速化を報告。

candidates.title: Large Flow Language Models
candidates.abstract: Continuous flow language models offer a path to parallel generation with tools for control and acceleration unavailable to discrete diffusion, yet effective techniques for building them at the billion-parameter scale remain less established. We present Lafa (Large flow language model), a fast, high-performing flow language model scaled to 8B parameters in a data-efficient manner. Lafa is a blockwise flow model with causal attention on the prefix and bidirectional, asynchronous flow within each block. This design enables efficient training by adapting pretrained autoregressive (AR) models and fast inference via prefix caching and blockwise parallel decoding. We train Lafa at 0.5B, 7B, and 8B scales with fewer than 30B tokens, more efficient than previous diffusion models, and evaluate it on instruction following, reasoning, and coding, where the learned flow matches or surpasses the quality of AR and can be distilled into flow maps for one- and few-step generation. Notably, flow training preserves or even improves pretrained AR capabilities via a multi-token prediction effect, which we leverage in a self-speculative decoding scheme that verifies flow-based drafts autoregressively within a single model. This yields 2.54x the throughput of an AR model at comparable quality, outperforming multi-token prediction and discrete diffusion methods. Our findings show that continuous flows can serve as a scalable foundation for language modeling.
candidates.reason: Lafaはprefix側を因果注意、block内を双方向非同期flowで処理する8B規模のcontinuous flow言語モデル。既存ARからの適応とprefix cache・block並列decodeで推論を高速化し、flow draftを同一モデルの自己回帰検証にかけるself-speculative方式を導入する。品質を保ちつつAR比2.54倍のthroughputを報告。

candidates.title: Batch-Paced: Fixed-Budget Batch Decoding in Discrete Diffusion Language Models
candidates.abstract: As generative language models become more capable and widely used, inference demand grows, making efficient serving increasingly important. Discrete diffusion language models (dLLMs) offer a promising path to more efficient inference through parallel token generation. Prior dLLM decoding methods, however, focus on improving inference efficiency for individual sequences. We formulate fixed-budget dLLM batch decoding and introduce Batch-Paced, a training-free method that jointly optimizes the allocation of decoding compute across requests to improve overall batch quality. Across two dLLM backbones, five benchmarks and their representative mixtures, Batch-Paced improves batch performance under matched budgets; gains generally grow with batch size and largely persist across decoding configurations. Analysis of requests'decoding trajectories suggests that these gains arise largely by raising the committed-token confidence of lower-confidence requests. We further show that Batch-Paced's batch decode time remains competitive and that adding a decoding-depth allowance during Batch-Paced decoding can shorten it further at a modest performance cost.
candidates.reason: Batch-Pacedは離散拡散LLMの複数要求に対し、固定のdecode計算予算を要求間で動的配分してbatch全体の品質を高める学習不要方式。2種類のbackbone・5ベンチマークと混合負荷で同一予算下の品質を改善し、batchが大きいほど効果が高まる傾向を報告。低信頼要求の確定token信頼度を上げる効果が主要因で、decode時間も競争的とする。
